offset.description: Line offset to start reading from

fs_write.description: Write or append content to a file. Creates parent directories automatically.

old_string.description: String to replace (required for patch mode)

fs_search.description: Search for files by glob pattern, search file contents with regex, OR run a structural AST search for symbols (functions, classes, methods, imports, calls, assignments) across Python/JS/TS.

pattern.description: Glob (mode=glob), regex (mode=content), or symbol name / fnmatch-glob (mode=ast)

context.description: Lines of context around each match (content/ast modes)

kind.description: AST-mode only: which kind of symbol to match

regex_name.description: AST-mode only: alternative to pattern, Python regex for symbol names

languages.description: AST-mode only: languages to scan (python, js, ts, jsx, tsx)

archive.description: Create, inspect, extract, or read single files from zip / tar / tar.gz / tar.bz2 / tar.xz archives. Path-traversal safe; size-capped to defuse zip bombs.

base_dir.description: Base dir for archive-relative names on create

fs_move.description: Move or rename a file or directory

run_python.description: Execute Python code in sandboxed subprocess and return stdout/stderr

run_bash.description: Execute bash command and return output

run_node.description: Execute Node.js code and return output

python_repl.description: Stateful Python REPL — unlike run_python, variables/imports/dataframes survive across calls per-session. Ideal for iterative data exploration.

code.description: Python code to run in the session

reset.description: Drop and recreate the session before running

web_fetch.description: Fetch a URL and return rich structured content: readability-cleaned main text (or markdown), title, description, author, publish date, Open Graph metadata, JSON-LD structured data, tables and top links. Handles HTML, JSON and PDFs. Use format='markdown' for nicely formatted extract, 'full' for everything, 'pdf' for PDFs.

max_chars.description: Max characters of content to return

web_search.description: Multi-engine web search (Google, Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Startpage, Yandex) in parallel with result merging and engine-agreement ranking. Full Google dorking supported either in the query string OR as structured args (site, exclude_site, filetype, intitle, inurl, intext, exact, or_terms, before, after). Example: query='best battery tech', site=['nature.com','arxiv.org'], after='2023-01-01'.

query.description: Search query — supports Google dork operators inline (site:, filetype:, intitle:, inurl:, "exact phrase", etc.)

site.description: Restrict to domain(s). String or array.

filetype.description: pdf | doc | xls | csv | ppt | txt | …

intitle.description: Phrase that must appear in title

inurl.description: Substring that must appear in URL

intext.description: Phrase that must appear in body

web_research.description: End-to-end research pipeline. Expands the topic into multiple sub-queries, searches across engines in parallel, ranks URLs by engine agreement and source quality (Wikipedia / news / academic prioritized, social noise filtered), fetches the top pages in parallel, extracts main content, and returns a structured dossier: sources, per-source excerpts, key bullet points, and extracted key facts with citations. This is the right tool when you actually need to answer a research question.

web_browse.description: Drive a headless Chromium (Playwright) to render a page with JavaScript, accept cookie banners, scroll to trigger lazy-loading, screenshot the result and return the fully rendered HTML plus extracted main text, metadata, visible images and links. Use when web_fetch returns too little (SPAs, JS-only content, lazy-loaded images).

image_search.description: Find and download high-quality images from the open web. Queries Google Images, Bing Images, DuckDuckGo Images, Yandex, Wikimedia Commons, Flickr, Pexels, Unsplash, Pixabay — in parallel. Editorial / news / wiki / real-photography sources rank first; generic stock is deprioritized. Pipeline auto-validates dimensions and magic bytes, deduplicates visually identical images with perceptual hashing, drops blurry ones, strips EXIF, and scores each for quality. Pick by quality — go for real, specific, editorial imagery rather than generic stock.

query.description: What to look for. Natural language; Google-style operators (site:, filetype:, "phrase") also accepted.

num_images.description: Number of final images to keep (1-25)

save_dir.description: Directory to save images (auto-created if empty)

avoid_stock.description: Deprioritize generic stock sources; prefer editorial/real photography

normalize.description: Convert webp/avif to jpg/png for broader compatibility

page_images.description: Scrape every image referenced by a single web page: +srcset (best variant), , CSS background-image, , og:image / twitter:image, JSON-LD image fields. Optionally downloads them with the same validation pipeline as image_search. Enable use_browser=true for heavy JS sites.

use_browser.description: Render with Playwright first (for JS-heavy sites)

http_request.description: Generic REST client. GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE with JSON / form / multipart bodies, bearer or basic auth, automatic retry with exponential backoff on 429/5xx, SSRF guard (refuses private/link-local IPs unless allow_private=true). Responses auto-parsed as JSON/text or flagged binary.

multipart.description: multipart/form-data body — each value may be a string or {path: ...}

save_to.description: If set, save raw body to this path

video_info.description: Video metadata + transcript extraction. YouTube: full metadata + transcripts (auto-generated and manual) with timestamps via the public timedtext API, optional on-the-fly translation, related videos. Vimeo: oEmbed metadata. Generic: Open Graph video metadata.

image_reverse.description: Reverse-image search against Yandex, Google Lens and Bing. Given a publicly hosted image URL, returns the pages where that image appears (source/context) plus visually similar images — useful for tracking down the original, finding higher-resolution versions, or identifying a subject.

path.description: Local file path (currently requires public URL — reserved for future upload support)

workspace_create.description: Create a new job workspace with structured directories

workspace_load.description: Load and summarize a workspace's current state

workspace_snapshot.description: Save a snapshot of current workspace state

workspace_list.description: List all workspaces with summary metadata (status, description, owner, created/modified times, optional size/file count). Filters by status and owner; respects per-user scoping when auth is on.

owner_id.description: Filter by owner; auto-set from env when auth is on

workspace_export.description: Bundle a workspace into a single zip or tar.gz archive with an embedded manifest (file list + sha256). Useful for sharing/archival. Size-capped and ownership-enforced.

memory_store.description: Store a key-value entry in memory (short or long term)

memory_get.description: Retrieve a memory entry by key

memory_search.description: Semantic search through stored memories. 3-layer fallback: sentence-transformers embeddings (cached) → hashed TF-IDF on character trigrams → token overlap. Combines semantic similarity with lexical overlap so both concepts and exact keywords surface.

min_score.description: Drop results below this combined score

agent_spawn.description: Spawn a sub-agent with a specific role to handle a subtask

context.description: Additional context to provide the agent

async_mode.description: Run agent asynchronously and return agent_id

job_id.description: Workspace job ID for the agent to work in

agent_status.description: Check status of a running async agent (instant, non-blocking)

agent_wait.description: Wait for an async agent to finish and return its result. Preferred over polling agent_status in a loop.

task_split.description: Decompose a complex task into an ordered list of subtasks with dependencies, parallel groups, and critical path. Classifies the task shape (research/build/fix/refactor/migrate/analyze/document/media/data/deploy) and composes from templates.

ast_search.description: Structural code search that understands syntax. Finds functions, classes, methods, imports, call sites, and assignments by walking Python ASTs / JS-TS structure regex (never plain text). Supports exact names, fnmatch globs, or regex.

name.description: Exact symbol name or fnmatch glob

languages.description: Subset of: python, js, ts, jsx, tsx

git_ops.description: Safe git wrapper: status, diff, log, branch, add, commit, checkout, push, pull, fetch, clone, remote, reset, stash, blame, show, ls_files. Destructive flags require explicit opt-in (force=true / allow_hard=true).

github_ops.description: GitHub REST v3 client. Works anonymously (60/hr) or with GITHUB_TOKEN (5000/hr, write access). Supports: repo_get, repo_search, user_get, list_issues, get_issue, create_issue, comment_issue, close_issue, list_prs, get_pr, create_pr, merge_pr, review_pr, get_file, list_dir, list_commits, get_commit, list_branches, list_tags, list_releases, get_release, workflow_runs, rate_limit.

code_analyzer.description: Analyze code structure, complexity, and patterns

repo_scanner.description: Scan a repository and produce structural overview

image_analyze.description: Advanced local image analysis tool. ALWAYS call this when the user sends an image or asks about image content. Uses PIL, numpy, OpenCV, and OCR to extract: dominant color palette with names and percentages, brightness/contrast/saturation metrics, full OCR text extraction (pytesseract + easyocr), edge density and sharpness, circle/shape/face detection, per-region 4x4 color and activity map, quadrant analysis, channel histograms, EXIF metadata, and image type classification. Returns a rich structured report that enables the AI to describe and reason about the image.

path.description: Absolute path to the saved image file

question.description: What to focus on or specific question about the image
question.default: Describe this image in full detail — content, style, colors, text, composition.

image_edit.description: Image manipulation via Pillow. Ops: info, resize, crop (box/center), rotate, flip, filter (blur/sharpen/edge/grayscale/sepia/invert/contour/emboss), adjust (brightness/contrast/saturation/gamma), watermark (text or image, positioned), compose (paste overlay), collage (grid), convert (format/quality), thumbnail, annotate (rectangles/circles/lines/text), pad.

pdf_generate.description: Generate PDFs from markdown, HTML, plain text, or a source file. Uses weasyprint when available for rich HTML/CSS rendering, falls back to reportlab. Supports title/author metadata, custom CSS, configurable page size and margins.

base_url.description: Base URL for resolving images (weasyprint only)

chart.description: Render charts as PNG / SVG / PDF via matplotlib. Types: line, area, bar (grouped or stacked, horizontal or vertical), scatter (optional sizes/colors/labels), pie, donut, histogram, heatmap, box. Data shape depends on type (see tool docstring).

colors.description: Color list or matplotlib colormap name

audio_transcribe.description: Transcribe audio / video with Whisper. Uses faster-whisper when available (4x faster, lower memory), falls back to openai-whisper. Auto language detection, optional translation to English, optional per-word timestamps, voice-activity detection.

data_query.description: Schema + query tool for CSV / TSV / Excel / Parquet / JSON / JSONL / SQLite files. Ops: schema (columns + types + null counts + samples), head, sample, stats (per-column), query (DuckDB if available, else SQLite in-memory), filter (pandas query), unique (distinct + counts), groupby, pivot, join.

expr.description: pandas query expression for filter op
